newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Brazil insurance market expected to boom.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brazil insurance market expected to boom.

text.p: Brazil's leading private insurer Sul America Seguros and U.S. insurance firm Aetna Inc have teamed up in expectation of a boom in the Brazilian insurance market, senior company officials said.

Aetna will acquire 49 percent of the joint venture, to be called Sul America Aetna, for 425 million reais (around $390 million). The new Sao Paulo based company will provide health, life and accident insurance as well as pension plans.
"The great explosion in this area will come with the reform of the social security system," Sul America Seguros President Rony Lyrio said.

"Another great pasture in Brazil will be the formation of savings. Personal savings are practically non-existant in Brazil, but with monetary stability this area will develop and we are betting on this," Lyrio said.
A constitutional reform of the social security system was approved by the Chamber of Deputies last year and is due to be rewritten in the Senate.

The joint venture, which is due to start in the second quarter of this year with an initial turnover of 1.6 billion reais ($1.54 billion), is expected to increase turnover 30 percent to more than 2 billion reais ($1.92 billion) by the end of the first financial year, Lyrio said.
Aetna Vice-Chairman Richard Huber said Aetna, which has other investments in Latin America, had waited until now to invest in Brazil because of economic conditions.
"We didn't invest because basic conditions like monetary stability and an open economy, which arrived in 1994, were lacking previously," he said.
Huber said large sums were invested in Brazilian public health insurance, but the returns to clients left much to be desired.

"We believe this is an excellent opportunity, especially in the health insurance sector, given the large number of Brazilians who would like to have access to quality health insurance, away from the public system," Huber said.

Aetna, which will provide product and marketing expertise, will pay an initial 330 million reais ($300 million) for its stake in the joint venture and the outstanding amount over a period of time based on future performance.
Lyrio said the joint venture was the biggest foreign investment in Brazil's financial area in 1996, representing five percent of all investments in the financial area.
Sul America Seguros is due to post its annual results this month with turnover expected to be 2.6 billion reais ($2.5 million), Lyrio said.
